newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Alusuisse reorganises, but no spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse reorganises, but no spinoff.

text.p: Swiss Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG on Friday dashed hopes that it would spin off an entire division and announced a new decentralised strategy for its reshaped operating divisions.

Under the new structure, developed under the leadership of new chief executive Sergio Marchionne, Alusuisse will sell off around eight companies in Britain, U.S. and Canada with combined sales of around 800 million Swiss francs ($546 million).
Marchionne said he expects to raise more than 500 million francs from the divestments, mostly in the packaging sector.

"This should be seen as an empowerment process of our businesses," Marchionne said of his plan to cut the influence of the central holding company, trim management layers and split each of the three operating divisions into two.
"Divisional spin-offs are not in the cards for our group," he said.
Alusuisse's shares, which had been bid up on speculation in the weeks prior to the news conference, tumbled and were down three percent at 1,445 francs in mid-afternoon trading.

Marchionne also announced new financial targets, including an average annual profit increase of 10 percent over the next five years and a rise in sales to 15 billion Swiss francs by 2002, up from 1996's 8.0 billion.
Acquisitions in pharmaceutical packaging, food flexibles and fine chemicals would help Alusuisse reach this goal.

Business volume so far this year has been relatively good and Marchionne confirmed that it still expects 1997 profit to surpass 1996's 417 million francs, despite poor results at the chemical sectors in the first five months of 1997.
Although he declined to be specific about his forecast, he said he was expressing some caution to the markets, given the problems in the chemicals sector.
The new structure flies in the face of the trend toward single-theme industrial groups, but Marchionne said Alusuisse never was a conglomerate and management was the key to success.
"We have reached the conclusion that this group should remain diversified and industrial, albeit managed along different lines," he said.

The news disappointed financial markets, where speculation had been rife that Marchionne's strategic review would result in a spin-off of one of its three divisions, a popular move used by many companies to unlock some of the hidden value.
Alusuisse's last reorganisation came in 1991 and led to a significant withdrawal from primary aluminium activities and to a series of acquisitions in the packaging area.

But Marchionne, whose background is in corporate finance, said the idea of creating "pure industrial entities" had little to do with how industrial companies operate and Alusuisse's future success lay in re-combining its current businesses in new sectors that reflected the true market activity.
Marchionne also wants to trim management so there are only a maximum of five layers between the group executive committee, which will be expanded, and the shop floor.
